final_answer:
Short answer: No, Client likely cannot stop paying, and Lessor is likely not responsible for the defective Trailers. Client's remedy lies against Manufacturer (now in Chapter 7), not Lessor.

1. Finance lease. Virginia's UCC Article 2A (Va. Code 8.2A-101 et seq.) governs. Under 8.2A-103(1)(g), a 'finance lease' is one where (i) the lessor does not select, manufacture or supply the goods; (ii) the lessor acquires the goods in connection with the lease; and (iii) one of several conditions is met, including that the lessee receives a copy of the supply contract before signing the lease. Here Client picked the model and negotiated the specs with Manufacturer, Lessor merely bought the Trailers for the lease and financed them, and Lessor gave Client a full copy of the purchase agreement before signing. I could not fetch the statutory text of 8.2A-103 itself (site blocked), so this element-by-element statement is from my knowledge of the uniform text and should be verified. The Lease is a commercial, not consumer, lease (a trucking company).

2. Irrevocable, independent promises. Va. Code 8.2A-407 provides that, in a finance lease that is not a consumer lease, the lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent on acceptance of the goods. This is self-executing, and the Lease's express 'absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or setoff' language reinforces it. The promises are enforceable by Lessor and its assignees and are not subject to cancellation or modification without consent. So Client's duty to pay rent survives the Trailers' compressor failures; the defects are not a defense to payment and Client cannot withhold or set off. Client's cessation of payment is therefore a default, exposing it to Lessor's default remedies under the Lease and Part 5 of Article 2A (acceleration if the Lease provides, repossession, damages), plus fees if provided. Whether Client 'accepted' the Trailers and whether revocation of acceptance is available against a finance lessor (8.2A-517/8.2A-516 context) was not researched; note that for finance leases 8.2A-407 conditions the irrevocability on acceptance, and Client appears to have accepted and used the Trailers for four months.

3. Lessor's liability. Va. Code 8.2A-209 extends to the lessee the benefit of the supplier's promises and warranties under the supply contract, to the extent of the lessee's leasehold interest, subject to the terms of the warranty and the supply contract and defenses. Thus Client takes the benefit of Manufacturer's two-year warranty directly and may assert it against Manufacturer, and Client retains any rights it has against Manufacturer by separate agreement or other law. That extension does not make the lessor a warrantor. Under Article 2A (8.2A-212 and 8.2A-213, which I did not verify here), the lessor's implied warranties of merchantability and fitness do not arise in a finance lease, and the Lease disclaims Lessor warranties and directs claims to Manufacturer. Lessor chose neither the Trailers nor their specifications, so there is no reliance-based fitness claim against it. Absent Lessor fraud, misrepresentation, or its own promises about the equipment, it bears no responsibility for defects.

4. Practical consequences. Client should (a) resume payments or negotiate with Lessor to cure; (b) file a proof of claim in Manufacturer's Chapter 7 case for breach of warranty (the trustee's refusal to perform the warranty makes this a general unsecured claim, likely of little value); (c) check for insurance, any third-party refrigeration unit maker (e.g., the compressor/unit supplier) warranty, which may be honored independently; (d) pursue self-help repair and damages claims against Manufacturer; (e) confirm the Lease for cure rights, notice and any provision allowing relief if the supplier fails. Possible exceptions: unconscionability (8.2A-108), Lessor's own misconduct, a Lessor-Manufacturer relationship that makes Lessor more than a financer, and defaults by Lessor in other obligations (e.g., quiet enjoyment). Also the Lease must be a true finance lease; if the Lessor is held to have 'supplied' or selected the goods, the hell-or-high-water protection under 8.2A-407 would not apply by statute, though the contractual waiver may still be enforced under general contract principles and 8.2A-103/8.2A-504. Caveats: I did not locate Virginia case law applying 8.2A-407 within the research budget.

authorities.title: Irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: In a non-consumer finance lease, lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent upon acceptance; enforceable against the lessee by lessor and assignees; self-executing.

authorities.title: Lessee under finance lease as beneficiary of supply contract
authorities.proposition: Lessee gets the benefit of supplier's promises and warranties under the supply contract to the extent of its leasehold interest, subject to the supply contract terms and defenses; does not impose supplier duties on lessee.

authorities.title: Definitions: finance lease
authorities.proposition: Finance lease elements: lessor does not select, manufacture or supply; acquires goods in connection with the lease; lessee receives supply contract copy before signing (or other alternative conditions).

claims.text: The arrangement is a finance lease because Lessor did not select or supply the Trailers, bought them for the lease, and gave Client the supply contract before signing.
Under 8.2A-407 and the Lease clause, Client's rent obligation is irrevocable and independent, so the defects do not excuse payment and Client's stopping payment is a default.

Client has the benefit of Manufacturer's warranty directly under 8.2A-209, but Lessor is not a warrantor and is not responsible for the Trailers' defects; recourse is against Manufacturer's bankruptcy estate.
